Subject: Production shortfall during peak — request for eligibility and evidence

Hi Jordan,

We hit a significant availability regression on our Redwood route (model: redwood-4b-v2) between 2029-03-14T02:47:10Z and 2029-03-14T02:58:36Z (UTC). During that ~11 minute window we saw ~40% 503s on checkout calls which caused multiple retries and 8 downstream failed payments.

We filed an SLO claim per section 4.2 of our contract and attached a short summary and the request for raw traces. Can you confirm whether this window is eligible for a credit (we're looking for downtime confirmation and, if eligible, a pro-rated credit per the hosted SLA)?

Attached: slo-claim-030429.pdf (summary, request form).

Jordan / team — pulled the bundles and ran a preliminary correlation. Summary below:

Observed window (UTC): 2029-03-14T02:46:58Z → 2029-03-14T02:59:02Z (approx 12m 4s)
Indicators:
- Rapid increase in preemption events on pool-gpu-7 (node scale-up/eviction traces show controller preempted two pods at 02:47:03Z and 02:49:18Z).
- Route-level 503 spike aligns exactly with the eviction + fallback routing (requests that hit evicted pods retried and some hit a warmup path causing 503 responses).
- No customer-side malformed requests observed.

Attachments: raw-traces-orchard-20290314.tar.gz (router logs, pod events, kernel eviction traces) — attached to this thread.

Prelim conclusion: impact window confirmed. Cause appears to be aggressive node preemption combined with insufficient prefix cache warmup for the fallback variant. We're compiling the full timeline and will produce a postmortem draft.

Next steps:
- I'll push an anonymized trace sample and a short evidence bundle to shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-orchard-traces
- Vanessa, can you prepare the SLA eligibility calc (per-hosted SLA terms) and confirm whether the event qualifies (I believe it does, but will confirm policy edge cases re: scheduled maintenance exclusions).

Irene
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2029 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production shortfall during peak — confirmation and next steps (Orchard Payments)

Samir — quick update and next actions from Redwood. Thanks again for flagging this.

What we confirmed:
- Impact window: 2029-03-14T02:46:58Z → 2029-03-14T02:59:02Z UTC (12m 4s) — verified by router and eviction traces.
- Root cause (prelim): controller-driven preemption on pool-gpu-7 which caused active pods to be evicted; fallback routing to a warmup variant caused transient 503s while prefix cache warmed.
- This event appears to meet the hosted SLA definition of "unavailable" (not scheduled maintenance, not customer-initiated).

What we will deliver:
1) Formal eligibility decision and pro-rated credit calculation based on the confirmed downtime (will include exact formula and contract reference).
2) Postmortem draft (timeline, RCA, mitigation plan) in ~5 business days.
3) Short-term mitigation steps we've already applied: reduced preemption aggressiveness on pool-gpu-7, adjusted warmup strategy for fallback variant, added a targeted cache seeding rule for high-QPS routes.

Attachments: raw-traces-orchard-20290314.tar.gz (evidence bundle) — public Drive link above.

If you'd like a working session with SRE to walk through traces, propose Tuesday at 10:00 PT (I'll include Vanessa & Irene).

Best,
